summary.text: A previously healthy 31-year-old man underwent right eye pars plana vitrectomy with silicone oil tamponade for traumatic retinal detachment and received postoperative topical and oral therapy. On postoperative day 18 he had right eye redness, pain and raised intraocular pressure with secondary glaucoma; steroid drops were stopped and brinzolamide 1% twice daily was started.

On day 6 of brinzolamide use he developed high fever up to 40°C and rashes on both upper limbs that progressed to widespread erythema, bullae, mucosal erosions and epidermal detachment, positive Nikolsky sign and asymmetric ocular findings. Admission tests showed leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, high CRP, abnormal liver enzymes, hypoalbuminemia and positive blood and wound cultures; SCORTEN was 2.

SJS/TEN overlap syndrome was confirmed from the clinical picture, positive Nikolsky sign, histopathology and BSA involvement over 30%, with brinzolamide considered the likely culprit (Naranjo 7, ALDEN 5). He received intravenous immunoglobulin, methylprednisolone, vancomycin with imipenem, voriconazole, albumin, electrolyte replacement, wound care and amniotic membrane transplantation.

By week 4 the skin lesions had largely healed with residual hyperpigmentation and scarring. The left eye developed symblepharon and corneal scarring and needed penetrating keratoplasty, after which visual acuity improved to 0.05, while the right eye remained without light perception because of the earlier retinal detachment.
